bullets.title: COHR: Citi raises PT to $440, MS Equal-weight $325 — $20B NPO LTA and 45% GM target drive bull case
bullets.body: Citi raised PT to $440 (from $420) on 30x FY2028E EPS of ~$16.5, citing Sep-Q revenue of $2.37B and EPS of $2.09 beating Street, Dec-Q guidance of $2.55–2.75B ~$110M above consensus, and a ~$20B 5-year NPO LTA with a major AI datacenter customer. Management raised long-term gross margin target to 45%+ (from 42%) by end of CY2028, with datacenter revenue +85% YoY and FY2027 pro forma revenue growth guided above 60%. Morgan Stanley stays Equal-weight at $325, valuing at ~21x FY2028E EPS, noting the LTA starts CY28 and flagging AI valuation correction as key risk.

bullets.title: APP: Big Q3 beat, 2027 EBITDA guide $9-10B (+10% vs Street); PT raised across shops
bullets.body: APP delivered its strongest topline beat in 6 quarters with Q3 revenues +55% YoY and 84% EBITDA margins, driven by the new Axon 2.0 model rollout and gaming up nearly 50% YoY. FY2027 Adj. EBITDA guidance of $9.0–10.0B came in 10%+ above Street's $8.6B; Q4 guide implies +10% QoQ growth. Piper raised PT to $355 (from $325, Neutral); GS TMT noted a $3.2B buyback announced alongside results.

bullets.title: U (Unity): Blowout Q3 and Q4 guide — Strategic revenue +31% QoQ, 4Q guide 42% above Street EBITDA
bullets.body: Unity reported Q3 Strategic revenue of $597M (+9% above consensus) and Adj. EBITDA of $257M (+38% above consensus), with Vector revenue +40% QoQ and +126% YoY. Q4 guidance of $683–691M revenue and $290–295M EBITDA came in 15% and 42% above Street respectively. Citi maintains Buy with $48 PT (13% upside from $42.46).

bullets.title: ARM: Revenue beat on licensing but royalties missed; FY27-28 Silicon AGI CPU target raised to $2B
bullets.body: ARM F2Q27 beat sales by ~5% and EPS by ~8% on 3 new ATAs and 4 CSS deals, with datacenter royalties doubling YoY for the third straight quarter. However, mobile royalties missed and overall royalty revenue of $670M came below GS/Street. Management raised AGI CPU revenue guidance to up to $2B across FY27/FY28 (prior >$1B), with H1 next year seen as the catalyst. Piper cut PT to $270 (from mid-30s multiple to 30x); GS rates Sell at $160 PT; Citi rates Buy citing pullback as enhanced entry.

bullets.title: SNAP: Q3 ad revenue slowed to +4% YoY vs +9% in Q2; DAUs missed; stock -10% pre-mkt
bullets.body: SNAP's Q3 advertising revenue decelerated sharply to +4% YoY from +9% in Q2, with DAUs below Street estimates. Subscription revenues were a bright spot at +84% YoY. The stock traded down ~10.5% in pre-market. Jefferies noted SNAP trades at 5x FY28 EBITDA vs. peers at 7x.

bullets.title: EXPE: Strong Q3 (room nights +6.9%, EBITDA $1.69B) but Q4 guide 7% below Street EBITDA; stock -7-8%
bullets.body: Expedia beat Q3 gross bookings at $34.0B (vs $33.0B est) and EBITDA of $1.69B with ~150bps margin upside, raising FY26 margin expansion guide to 180–200bps. However, Q4 guidance came 1% below consensus on gross bookings and 7% below on EBITDA, attributed to U.S. election cycle, EMEA disruption, and higher B2B partner promotions. KeyBanc maintains Sector Weight; stock was down ~7–8% pre-market.

bullets.title: HUBS: Q4 revenue guide collapsed to 12% YoY vs Street expectation; FY26 guidance cut to $945-947M
bullets.body: HubSpot guided Q4 revenue at ~12% YoY growth, well below Street, and cut full-year FY26 revenue guidance to $945–947M vs Street's $965M as demand deteriorates and net customer additions fell to ~5,250 vs. 7,000 prior quarter. Stock was down ~8% pre-market. Jefferies noted this as the standout negative in a mixed software earnings week.

bullets.title: CORZ: UBS Buy — Q3 beats across the board; CoreWeave Dalton on track for early 2027
bullets.body: Core Scientific reported Q3 revenues of $233M (vs UBS $224M, Street $199M), Adj. EBITDA of $134M (vs UBS $100M, Street $81M), and colocation gross margins of 88% ex-power (up from 83%). Billable IT capacity reached 485MW from 395MW. CoreWeave Dalton site on track for full delivery in early 2027; blended NOI margins across leases expected at ~90%. UBS maintains Buy.

bullets.title: CSCO: Morgan Stanley downgrades to Equal-Weight, cuts PT to $120 on pullforward risk and AI margin pressure
bullets.body: MS downgraded Cisco from Overweight to Equal-Weight, cutting PT from $135 to $120, after the stock rallied 43% over the past 12 months vs. S&P +14% and rerated to parity at ~19x forward earnings (vs. historical 20% discount). Key concerns are VAR pullforward similar to FFIV/FTNT, and AI cloud orders coming at 30–40% hardware margins vs. higher enterprise margins. MS expects FQ1 revenue of ~$18.3–18.4B and FY27 guidance raise to ~$73.25B, but sees limited EPS leverage from AI mix.

bullets.title: CHTR: Morgan Stanley cuts PT to $135, warns Cox KPIs weaker than expected amid fiber/FWA pressure
bullets.body: MS reduced CHTR PT from $140 to $135 (5x forward EV/EBITDA) after Cox KPI disclosures revealed steeper residential broadband subscriber losses than legacy Charter. FY27 consolidated estimates cut -1% revenue/-1% EBITDA/-2% FCF/sh, with Cox cut -5% on both. Verizon's new 1Gbps FWA mmWave solution expanding addressable market by 10–15M homes, and aggressive fiber offers at $30–40/month intensifying competition. MS views CHTR as having the weakest medium-term growth algorithm in US Telco/Cable.

bullets.title: TKO: MS reiterates OW $230 PT — WWE partnerships +28% YoY, UFC margins +400bps, guide raised
bullets.body: TKO raised FY26 revenue guide by $10M to $5.81B and Adj. EBITDA by $15M to $2.305B. WWE Partnership revenues accelerated +28% YoY in Q3 with +50% guided for Q4; UFC 329 grossed a record $26M gate with McGregor return driving 16M viewers. MS raises buyback estimate to $1.4B from $1.2B for CY26, projects $1.2B global partnerships revenue target by 2030, and expects FY27 EBITDA +8% with 300bps margin expansion. PT based on 25x forward FCF.

bullets.title: NYT: Digital net adds re-accelerated to 420K in Q3, but ad growth disappointed and Q4 expenses raised
bullets.body: The New York Times saw digital-only net adds of 420K in Q3, well ahead of ~200K expectation, with subscription revenue +10.7% YoY. Advertising disappointed at +7.8% vs. high-single/low-double digit guidance, and Q4 expense guidance was raised 6–8% (vs prior ~6%) due to video investment. Morgan Stanley maintains Equal-weight at $75 PT; JPM noted AI Overviews/AI Mode as a potential headwind to ad revenue going forward.

bullets.title: AMPL: DA Davidson raises PT to $21; Q3 revenue accelerated to +25% YoY, Statsig acquisition broadens TAM
bullets.body: Amplitude's Q3 revenue growth accelerated to 25% YoY vs. 21% in Q2, driven by data upselling (now 90% of contracted entitlements vs. 85%), higher ASPs, and longer contract duration. The Statsig acquisition adds experimentation and AI agent analytics, broadening the TAM beyond product analytics. DA Davidson raises PT to $21 (5.5x '27 revenue); Piper raised PT to $22, calling AMPL one of the best acceleration/turnaround stories YTD.

bullets.title: AMPL: Revenue acceleration to 25% YoY, Statsig acquisition, PT raised to $21-$22
bullets.body: Amplitude Q3 revenue growth accelerated to 25% YoY from 21% in Q2, with QoQ ARR up $21M on higher ASPs and longer contracts. The Statsig acquisition broadens the TAM into AI agent analytics. DA Davidson raised PT to $21 (5.5x '27 revenue vs. 7x for 20%+ growth peers); Piper raised to $22. Q4 guide implies slight decel to +23% YoY; analysts confident in 2027 durability.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure/datacenter trade unwind post-midterms — TX/GA moratorium risks spook semis complex
bullets.body: Post-midterm election results triggered a sharp unwind in AI infrastructure names: TX (27% of MW in high-yield DC funding), GA, and NM governors proposed datacenter moratoriums, putting 62+ GW of 2028 capacity in question per JPM. Buildout baskets fell from -1% to -11% while non-AI cyclicals (Homebuilders +8%, Retailers +5.5%) rallied. Hedge funds rotated toward Software/SaaS (+1.6σ) and hyperscalers (+1.1σ) away from hardware/memory; AMD -5%, MU -4.7%, DELL -5% pre-market.

bullets.title: MRVL + LITE merger: combined silicon-optics solution for XPU architectures; combined -40% since announcement
bullets.body: Jefferies noted the MRVL-LITE merger rationale as a combined silicon-optics solution optimized for scale-up/scale-in XPU architectures, but the combined decline since the deal announcement is approaching 40%. LITE was down ~4.6% pre-market in the broader semis selloff.

bullets.title: GLW: Fox Advisors upgrades to Outperform from Equal-weight
bullets.body: Fox Advisors analyst Steven Fox upgraded Corning to Outperform from Equal-weight with the stock at $118.77. GLW was down ~4% pre-market in the broader tech selloff.

bullets.title: AMZN: +2.3% pre-market on $0 delivery fee for Prime members via Uber Eats partnership
bullets.body: Amazon announced a $0 delivery fee for Prime members ordering via Uber Eats, driving AMZN up ~2.3% and UBER higher pre-market. The deal reinforces Amazon's Prime value proposition and expands Uber Eats' addressable subscriber base.

bullets.title: NXST: Citi Buy, $215 PT — Q3 revenue 3% above consensus, EBITDA 5% above; 20% total return expected
bullets.body: Nexstar reported Q3 revenue of $2,133M (+3% vs consensus) and Adj. EBITDA of $756M (+5% vs consensus). Citi maintains Buy with $215 PT vs. current ~$186, implying 15.8% price upside and 20% total return including 4.2% dividend. Key overhang remains TEGNA acquisition risks (potential divestitures incorporated as $32 downside in PT).

bullets.title: Upcoming catalysts: CPI Nov 10, CSCO/TTD/CRWV earnings; Microsoft Ignite Nov 17-20
bullets.body: Key macro: CPI due Nov 10 at 8:30am ET, PPI Nov 13. Earnings reporters next week include CSCO, TTD, CRWV, HIMS, CEG, QBTS, RGTI. Microsoft Ignite conference Nov 17–20 in SF and AWS re:Invent Nov 30–Dec 4 are the next major tech catalysts. Fed meeting scheduled Dec 9.
